macro: US equity indices are mixed at midday with the SPX flat, Nasdaq up 38 basis points, R2K up 30 basis points, and the Dow down 43 basis points. Markets are in a holding pattern as investors await developments at the UN regarding Iran and the Middle East, with Brent crude off modestly near $100 on hopes for a diplomatic resolution and the partial resumption of Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline. Treasuries are largely flat across the curve, while gold, silver, and bitcoin are all slightly lower.
rates_fed: Treasuries are pretty flat across the curve with no major rate moves driving the session. There is no notable Fed commentary cited in today's update. The macro backdrop is more geopolitically driven than rates-driven today.
market_outlook: Neutral to cautiously optimistic lean — the market is treading water ahead of a dense AI catalyst window over the next 10 days, including Zuckerberg's Meta Connect keynote Wednesday night, OpenAI's DevDay on September 29th, and Micron earnings on September 30th. The key catalyst to watch today is any diplomatic signal out of the UN on Iran and the Strait of Hormuz.
bull_case: Iran has reportedly offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US takes initial steps to ease military pressure, and Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline appears to be coming partially back online, which could relieve oil supply pressure. AI enthusiasm remains elevated ahead of a major catalyst cluster — Meta Connect, OpenAI DevDay, and Micron earnings — with Meta's Muse agent seeing surging downloads and Shopify integrating it for agentic checkout. Pockets of tech, housing, travel, and consumer staples are all showing strength, suggesting the market has enough underlying demand to hold levels.
bear_case: Financials are broadly underperforming with banks, brokers, insurers, and asset managers all in the red, which is a notable drag and could signal risk-off rotation beneath the surface. CMS lab payment rate cuts larger than anticipated are hitting Quest and LabCorp, and managed care names are also weak, pointing to healthcare sector headwinds. Texas Governor Abbott halting data center permitting adds regulatory risk to the AI infrastructure buildout, and SB Energy's delayed IPO due to investor pushback on valuation suggests sentiment on the data center boom may be cooling at the margin.

company_items.summary: AutoZone reported fiscal Q4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — tariff refunds added 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash LIFO impact added another 105 basis points. Domestic comps came in at +1.6% versus the Street's +3.1%, though management noted positive comp linearity, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year over year.

MillerKnoll reported solid fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and critically the beat holds up even excluding tariff refunds — stripping out the 11-cent tailwind, EPS was still 42 cents versus the Street's 36 cents. Guidance is mixed with fiscal 2027 sales range trimmed but EPS outlook left unchanged.

THOR Industries missed fiscal Q4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, as gross margin weakness — down 230 basis points year over year to 12.4% versus the Street's 13.85% — more than offset slightly better-than-expected revenue of $2.311 billion versus $2.17 billion expected. Management cited a difficult macro landscape.

Meta's Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads ahead of Zuckerberg's keynote at Meta Connect Wednesday night, and Shopify has agreed to allow Muse to complete purchases on its e-commerce platform. Amazon has blocked Muse from its platform, but the Shopify integration and growing buzz are building bullish expectations into the event.

Shopify announced it will allow Meta's Muse personal AI agent to complete purchases on its e-commerce platform, a meaningful agentic commerce partnership. This stands in contrast to Amazon's decision to block Muse, potentially giving Shopify a competitive edge in the emerging AI-agent shopping channel.

Quest Diagnostics shares were hit after CMS released new Medicare payment rates for lab services that represented a larger reduction than the market had anticipated. The rate cuts are a direct headwind to revenue and margins for lab testing firms.

Labcorp is down alongside Quest Diagnostics following new CMS Medicare lab payment rates that came in worse than expected. Both lab testing companies face a meaningful reimbursement headwind from the larger-than-anticipated rate cuts.

Cognex announced it will acquire RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. The deal positions Cognex more aggressively in the Physical AI and robotics space.

Viking Therapeutics reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in the trial data. This is a meaningful clinical milestone that reinforces VK2735 as a competitive asset in the crowded but high-stakes obesity drug market.

On Holdings held its analyst day and outlined 2029 sales targets of at least CHF 5.6 billion versus the Street's CHF 5.4 billion, with EBITDA margins of 22% or better versus the Street's 21% estimate. The company also adopted a $1 billion share buyback authorization, adding a capital return angle to the growth story.

sectors: Financials broadly underperforming — banks, brokers, insurers, and asset managers all in the red. Healthcare mixed with lab testing (DGX, LH) hit hard by CMS rate cuts and managed care weak, while medical devices and select biotech outperform. Tech is bifurcated with AI-adjacent semis and infrastructure names (ARM, ASML, MU, ORCL, META) outperforming while legacy enterprise tech (ACN, ADBE, CRM, MSFT, NOW) lags. Housing (DHI, LEN, PHM), travel/leisure, and consumer staples are pockets of strength. Aerospace and defense is broadly lower. Data center infrastructure faces new regulatory risk from Texas Governor Abbott halting permitting for new projects.

tts_summary: Here's your midday update for Tuesday September 22nd. Markets are treading water. The S&P 500 is essentially flat, the Nasdaq is up about 38 basis points, the Russell 2000 is up 30 basis points, and the Dow is the laggard, off 43 basis points. Treasuries are flat across the curve. Brent crude is hovering near 100 dollars a barrel, off modestly, as investors watch developments at the United Nations around Iran and the Middle East. The headline geopolitical note is that Iran has reportedly offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US takes initial steps to ease military pressure — that's a meaningful potential catalyst if it develops. Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline also appears to be partially coming back online after Houthi and Iran-aligned militia disruptions forced crude back through the Strait. On the company side, AutoZone beat fiscal Q4 earnings at 56.05 versus the Street's 54.03, but it was a low-quality beat — tariff refunds and a non-cash inventory accounting benefit drove most of the upside while domestic comparable sales missed significantly, coming in at plus 1.6 percent versus the Street's plus 3.1 percent. MillerKnoll was the cleaner earnings story — they beat at 53 cents versus 36 cents expected, and critically the beat holds even without tariff refunds. THOR Industries missed on margins and management cited a tough macro environment. Viking Therapeutics is getting attention after reporting 22 percent weight loss in its GLP-1 trial — that's a strong data point in the obesity drug race. On Meta, the Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads ahead of Zuckerberg's Connect keynote tomorrow night, and Shopify just announced it will allow Muse to complete purchases on its platform — that's a meaningful contrast to Amazon blocking it. Lab testing names Quest Diagnostics and Labcorp are under real pressure after CMS released Medicare payment rate cuts for lab services that were larger than the market expected. Cognex is buying RealSense, the leader in depth-sensing cameras for Physical AI and robotics, for roughly 500 million dollars upfront. On Holdings had a strong analyst day, raising its 2029 sales target above consensus and announcing a one billion dollar buyback. Sector-wise, financials are broadly weak across banks, brokers, insurers, and asset managers. AI-adjacent semis and infrastructure are outperforming. Housing, travel, and consumer staples are holding up well. The big directional call here is simple — the market is in a holding pattern, waiting on two things: any diplomatic signal out of the UN on Hormuz and the Iran situation, and the AI catalyst cluster kicking off tomorrow night with Zuckerberg's keynote, followed by OpenAI's developer day on the 29th and Micron earnings on the 30th. If you get positive resolution on the geopolitical front and Zuckerberg delivers tomorrow, you have a real setup for a leg higher in AI names. The bear risk is that financials are flashing something the headline indices aren't, and the Texas data center permitting halt plus a cooling IPO market for AI infrastructure suggest the easy money in that trade may be getting harder to justify at current valuations.
